title: Nahum Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Nahum chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Nahum Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Nahum Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Nahum 2:1, what are you instructed to do when the one that dashes in pieces comes up before your face?
options: Keep the munition, watch the way, make your loins strong, fortify your power mightily
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the munition, watch the way, make your loins strong, fortify your power mightily
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:1 instructs to keep the munition, watch the way, make the loins strong, and fortify power mightily when the one who dashes in pieces comes up before your face.

questions.question: In Nahum 2:2, what has the LORD turned away from Jacob and Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: The excellency
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:2 states that the LORD hath turned away the excellency of Jacob and Israel.

questions.question: What color are the shields of the mighty men as described in Nahum 2:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Red
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:3 describes the shield of his mighty men as made red.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:3 mentions that the valiant men wear scarlet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:3 says the valiant men are in scarlet, confirming the statement is true.

questions.question: According to Nahum 2:4, how do the chariots run?
questions.correctAnswer: Like the lightnings
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:4 states the chariots shall run like the lightnings.

questions.question: What do the chariots do in the streets in Nahum 2:4?
options: They justle one against another in the broad ways
questions.correctAnswer: They justle one against another in the broad ways
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:4 describes the chariots raging in the streets and justling one against another in the broad ways.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:5 says the worthies shall walk without stumbling.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:5 states the worthies shall stumble in their walk, so the statement is false.

questions.question: What will the worthies do according to Nahum 2:5 after stumbling in their walk?
options: Make haste to the wall and the defence shall be prepared
questions.correctAnswer: Make haste to the wall and the defence shall be prepared
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:5 says the worthies will stumble, then make haste to the wall, and the defence shall be prepared.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:6 says the gates of the rivers shall be closed tightly.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:6 actually says the gates of the rivers shall be opened, thus the statement is false.

questions.question: What happens to the palace according to Nahum 2:6?
questions.correctAnswer: The palace shall be dissolved
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:6 clearly states the palace shall be dissolved.

questions.question: Who is led away captive according to Nahum 2:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Huzzab
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:7 says Huzzab shall be led away captive.

questions.question: In Nahum 2:8, what is said about Nineveh?
options: It is like a pool of water
It is like a burning fire
questions.correctAnswer: It is like a pool of water
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:8 describes Nineveh as of old like a pool of water.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:8 says that when they cry 'Stand, stand', many will look back.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:8 says they shall cry 'Stand, stand' but none shall look back, so the statement is false.

questions.question: What is the state of Nineveh described in Nahum 2:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Empty, void, and waste
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:10 states that Nineveh is empty, void, and waste.

questions.question: In Nahum 2, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Keep the munition, watch the way, make thy loins strong
Take ye the spoil of silver and gold
Make haste to the wall and prepare the defence
Open the gates of the rivers
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the munition, watch the way, make thy loins strong
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:1 gives the instruction to keep the munition, watch the way, and make the loins strong before any other listed instructions appear in the chapter.

medium.title: Nahum Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Nahum Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will happen to the gates of the rivers and the palace according to Nahum 2:6?
options: The gates will be sealed and the palace fortified
The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace shall be dissolved
The gates will be guarded by angels and the palace protected
The gates will be closed and the palace expanded
questions.correctAnswer: The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace shall be dissolved
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:6 clearly states that the gates of the rivers shall be opened and the palace shall be dissolved, indicating a loss of protection and impending destruction. This connects with the following verses about captivity and flight (Nahum 2:7-8).

questions.question: Who is Huzzab described as in Nahum 2:7, and what happens to her?
options: A warrior who defends the city fiercely
A captive woman led away, with her maids making the sound of doves
A prophetess who warns the people
A queen who escapes the city
questions.correctAnswer: A captive woman led away, with her maids making the sound of doves
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:7 describes Huzzab being led away captive, with her maids accompanying her, making sounds like doves tabering on their breasts. This imagery portrays sorrow and captivity, connecting to the palace's dissolution in Nahum 2:6 and the flight described in Nahum 2:8.

questions.question: According to Nahum 2:8, how do the people of Nineveh respond when they flee?
options: They stand firm and fight back
They flee away shouting 'Stand, stand,' but none look back
They pray for mercy and protection
They hide quietly in their homes
questions.correctAnswer: They flee away shouting 'Stand, stand,' but none look back
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:8 describes the people of Nineveh fleeing while crying 'Stand, stand,' but no one looks back, showing panic and hopelessness. This follows the captivity mentioned in Nahum 2:7 and precedes the plundering in Nahum 2:9.

questions.question: What does Nahum 2:9 teach about the wealth of Nineveh?
options: The city has little wealth and no spoil to take
The spoil of silver and gold is abundant with no end to the store and glory
The wealth is hidden and cannot be taken
The wealth belongs to the poor and will be protected
questions.correctAnswer: The spoil of silver and gold is abundant with no end to the store and glory
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:9 reveals that the spoil of silver and gold is vast and without end, emphasizing the richness of Nineveh's possessions. This contrasts with the desolation described in Nahum 2:10 and highlights the completeness of the city's plunder.

questions.question: How does Nahum 2:10 describe the emotional and physical state of the people after the city's fall?
options: They are empty, void, with hearts melting, knees smiting, pain in loins, and faces gathering blackness
They gather to rebuild with hope
questions.correctAnswer: They are empty, void, with hearts melting, knees smiting, pain in loins, and faces gathering blackness
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:10 portrays the people’s extreme distress and fear after the fall of Nineveh, showing emotional and physical suffering. This follows the plundering described in Nahum 2:9 and connects to the helplessness described in Nahum 2:8.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:6–7 together depict the opening of the gates as a sign of freedom for Nineveh's inhabitants.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:6 mentions the gates of the rivers being opened and the palace dissolved, while Nahum 2:7 describes Huzzab being led away captive. Together, these verses show downfall and captivity, not freedom.

questions.question: What practical lesson about vigilance can Christians learn from Nahum 2:1 in light of Nahum 2:6's prediction of gates opening and palace dissolving?
options: To ignore warnings and trust in worldly security
To keep strong and watchful, as downfall can come suddenly
To rely solely on physical defenses
To expect no opposition or attack
questions.correctAnswer: To keep strong and watchful, as downfall can come suddenly
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:1 urges to keep the munition and watch the way, making strength mighty, which aligns with the sudden opening of gates and palace dissolving in Nahum 2:6. This teaches Christians the importance of spiritual vigilance and readiness.

questions.question: How does Nahum 2:9 encourage believers regarding generosity and stewardship?
options: It suggests hoarding wealth for personal safety
It shows that wealth is temporary and can be taken, encouraging generous stewardship
It promotes ignoring material possessions entirely
It advises investing only in earthly treasures
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that wealth is temporary and can be taken, encouraging generous stewardship
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:9 describes the vast spoil of silver and gold being taken, reminding believers that earthly wealth is temporary and can be lost. This can encourage a biblical attitude of generosity and wise stewardship of resources.

questions.question: According to Nahum 2:7-8, what does the imagery of maids tabering upon their breasts like doves signify about the atmosphere during Nineveh's fall?
questions.correctAnswer: Sorrow, mourning, and lamentation
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:7 uses the sound of doves tabering upon their breasts, a biblical symbol of mourning and lamentation, which reflects the sorrowful atmosphere during Nineveh’s fall as described alongside the flight in Nahum 2:8.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:10 describes the people’s reaction to the city's destruction as calm and hopeful.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:10 describes the people as empty, void, with hearts melting, knees smiting, pain in loins, and faces gathering blackness, indicating fear and despair rather than calm or hope.

questions.question: What does Nahum 2:8 teach about human response in times of crisis?
options: People will stand firm and fight to the end
People may panic and flee without looking back
People will seek wise counsel and plan carefully
People will trust in their own strength exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: People may panic and flee without looking back
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:8 shows the people crying 'Stand, stand' but fleeing away without looking back, illustrating panic and fear in crisis. This warns believers to maintain faith and trust in God rather than panic.

questions.question: In light of Nahum 2:6-7, what biblical virtue is illustrated by the downfall and captivity of Nineveh?
options: Humility and submission to God's judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and submission to God's judgment
questions.explanation: The opening of the gates and captivity of Huzzab in Nahum 2:6-7 illustrate God's judgment on Nineveh, teaching believers the importance of humility and submission to God’s authority to avoid similar downfall.

questions.question: How does Nahum 2:9-10 together teach about the consequences of sin and divine judgment?
options: Sin leads to endless riches and joy
Divine judgment results in loss, emptiness, and despair
Sin is ignored and has no consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment results in loss, emptiness, and despair
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:9 describes the taking of spoil, and Nahum 2:10 describes the resulting emptiness and despair, showing that divine judgment leads to loss and suffering, warning believers to live righteously.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:7 describes the captives as being led away with joy and celebration.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:7 describes Huzzab being led away captive and the maids making the sound of doves tabering on their breasts, an image of mourning, not joy or celebration.

questions.question: How can Nahum 2:6-8 be applied to Christians facing spiritual attacks?
options: To prepare defenses, stay vigilant, and not be overcome by fear
To ignore the attacks and pretend all is well
questions.correctAnswer: To prepare defenses, stay vigilant, and not be overcome by fear
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:6-8 shows gates opening and flight in fear, but earlier verses like Nahum 2:1 urge vigilance and strength. Christians can apply this by preparing spiritually and trusting God rather than succumbing to fear.

hard.title: Nahum Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Nahum Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Nahum 2:11, what is described as the 'dwelling' and 'feedingplace'?
questions.correctAnswer: Lions
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:11 directly refers to the 'dwelling of the lions' and the 'feedingplace of the young lions,' indicating lions as the subject.

questions.question: According to Nahum 2:12, what did the lion do for its whelps and lionesses?
options: Tore in pieces enough for his whelps and strangled for his lionesses
Fed them with honey and milk
questions.correctAnswer: Tore in pieces enough for his whelps and strangled for his lionesses
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:12 states that the lion tore in pieces enough for his whelps and strangled for his lionesses, illustrating the lion's strength and provision.

questions.question: What does the LORD declare He will do to the chariots in Nahum 2:13?
options: Burn her chariots in the smoke
questions.correctAnswer: Burn her chariots in the smoke
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:13 says, 'I will burn her chariots in the smoke,' indicating divine judgment and destruction of the military power symbolized by the chariots.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of divine judgment against proud cities as seen in Nahum 2:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 10:12
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:12 speaks of the LORD's judgment on Assyria, similar to Nahum 2:13's pronouncement against Nineveh, linking both as prophetic judgments on proud nations.

questions.question: According to Nahum 2:8, how is Nineveh described in relation to water?
questions.correctAnswer: Like a pool of water
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:8 describes Nineveh as 'of old like a pool of water,' suggesting calmness or stagnation before its impending destruction.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the gates of the rivers shall be opened' in Nahum 2:6?
options: Symbolizes a flood of enemies attacking
Means the city will experience drought
questions.correctAnswer: Symbolizes a flood of enemies attacking
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:6 uses the opening of 'gates of the rivers' metaphorically to represent the overwhelming invasion that will dissolve the palace defenses.

questions.question: Who is 'Huzzab' mentioned in Nahum 2:7 likely referring to?
options: A city or citadel of Nineveh
questions.correctAnswer: A city or citadel of Nineveh
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:7 mentions Huzzab being led captive, which scholars interpret as a part or district of Nineveh captured during the siege.

questions.question: What literary device is prominent in Nahum 2:4 where chariots 'shall seem like torches' and 'run like the lightnings'?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:4 uses similes comparing chariots to torches and lightning to vividly describe their speed and brightness.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'dasheth in pieces' in Nahum 2:1?
options: To break violently or dash to pieces
questions.correctAnswer: To break violently or dash to pieces
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root for 'dasheth' means to violently break or dash in pieces, fitting Nahum 2:1's description of an aggressive enemy approach.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:10 describes the city as full of joy and celebration.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:10 explicitly describes the city as 'empty, and void, and waste' with hearts melting and faces gathering blackness, indicating despair rather than joy.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 2:3 depicts the mighty men as wearing scarlet and their shields stained red.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:3 states that the shield of mighty men is made red and valiant men are in scarlet, portraying a vivid image of bloodied warriors.

questions.question: How does Nahum 2:13 relate to the New Testament's description of God's judgment?
options: It foreshadows the final judgment as described in Revelation 19
It contradicts the New Testament's message of grace
It only concerns Old Testament times and has no New Testament relevance
It portrays God as indifferent to nations
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the final judgment as described in Revelation 19
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:13's depiction of divine destruction echoes the final judgment imagery in Revelation 19 where God's wrath is executed against evil powers.

questions.question: What parallel theme exists between Nahum 2:2 and the book of Deuteronomy regarding Israel's state?
options: Both speak of the emptiness and downfall due to sin
Both describe Israel's prosperity and peace
Both focus on the wilderness journey
questions.correctAnswer: Both speak of the emptiness and downfall due to sin
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:2 describes the emptiness and loss of Jacob's excellency, paralleling Deuteronomy's warnings about Israel's downfall if they disobey God.

questions.question: What does Nahum 2:9 suggest about the wealth of Nineveh before its fall?
options: There was no end to the store and glory
questions.correctAnswer: There was no end to the store and glory
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:9 invites taking the spoil of silver and gold, stating there is no end of the store and glory, highlighting Nineveh's immense wealth.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar imagery of lions as used in Nahum 2:11-12?
questions.correctAnswer: Judges
questions.explanation: The book of Judges uses lion imagery (e.g., Samson and the lion) similarly to Nahum's depiction of lions representing strength and territory.

theological.title: Nahum Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Nahum Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily displayed in Nahum 2:1 through the command to "keep the munition, watch the way, make thy loins strong"?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence preparing for war
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:1 emphasizes the preparation for divine judgment by exhorting strength and vigilance, reflecting God's omnipotent control over the unfolding judgment. This is not about mercy or covenant faithfulness but about God's sovereign power to execute justice.

questions.question: According to Nahum 2:2, what is the theological significance of the LORD turning away the excellency of Jacob and Israel?
options: Judgment due to Israel's idolatry and rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment due to Israel's idolatry and rebellion
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:2 portrays the LORD turning away the excellency as a consequence of Israel's emptiers having emptied them, implying judgment for their sin rather than abandonment or blessing enemies.

questions.question: What does the imagery of "the shield of his mighty men is made red" and "chariots with flaming torches" in Nahum 2:3 signify about God's judgment?
options: The cleansing nature of God's judgment
The violent and consuming aspect of divine wrath
questions.correctAnswer: The violent and consuming aspect of divine wrath
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:3 uses vivid war imagery—red shields and flaming chariots—to depict the fierce and consuming nature of God's judgment against Nineveh, highlighting His righteous wrath.

questions.question: How does Nahum 2:4's description of chariots running like lightnings contribute to the understanding of God's judgment?
options: It shows the swift and unstoppable execution of judgment
It emphasizes the mercy of God
It highlights the uncertainty of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the swift and unstoppable execution of judgment
questions.explanation: The metaphor of chariots running like lightning in Nahum 2:4 portrays God's judgment as swift and inevitable, reinforcing His sovereign power to execute justice rapidly.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine protection and human failure is taught in Nahum 2:5 regarding the worthies stumbling and hastening to the wall?
options: Human strength cannot ultimately repel God's judgment
God guarantees victory to all armies
Walls are the ultimate source of safety
Judgment can be avoided by human effort
questions.correctAnswer: Human strength cannot ultimately repel God's judgment
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:5 shows that even the mightiest defenders stumble and rush to fortify defenses, illustrating that human efforts are insufficient against God's sovereign judgment.

questions.question: In Nahum 2:6, what does the opening of the gates of the rivers and the dissolution of the palace symbolize in the context of God's judgment?
options: The comprehensive destruction of political power and security
The renewal of the city under God's blessing
The establishment of a new kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The comprehensive destruction of political power and security
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:6 depicts the gates of rivers opening and the palace dissolving, symbolizing the total collapse of Nineveh’s political and royal security as part of divine judgment.

questions.question: What theological significance is found in Nahum 2:7's depiction of Huzzab being led captive with maids tabering upon their breasts?
options: The humiliation and mourning over the fall of a once-glorious city
The restoration of the city’s honor
questions.correctAnswer: The humiliation and mourning over the fall of a once-glorious city
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:7 describes Huzzab led captive with mourning sounds like doves' voices and tabering, symbolizing deep humiliation and lamentation due to the city's destruction.

questions.question: How does Nahum 2:8’s description of Nineveh as "like a pool of water" that flees contribute to the biblical narrative of judgment?
options: It illustrates the instability and inevitable collapse of worldly powers
It shows the eternal security of the city
It symbolizes the city's spiritual blessing
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the instability and inevitable collapse of worldly powers
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:8 uses the simile of a pool of water that flees to convey the fleeting and unstable nature of earthly kingdoms facing God’s judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine provision and judgment can be derived from the combined teachings of Nahum 2:9 and Nahum 2:10?
options: God’s judgment results in the loss of wealth and causes deep human suffering
God always preserves the riches of the wicked
God’s judgment is mild and restores quickly
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment results in the loss of wealth and causes deep human suffering
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:9 commands taking spoil of silver and gold, and Nahum 2:10 describes the city as empty and hearts melting with pain, teaching that God's judgment leads to loss and distress.

questions.question: In Nahum 2:11, the question about the dwelling and feeding place of lions serves what theological purpose?
options: To highlight the loss of power and security once enjoyed by Nineveh
To show the flourishing strength of the city
To reveal God's blessing on the city
To indicate the city's growth in righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: To highlight the loss of power and security once enjoyed by Nineveh
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:11 asks where the lions once fearless now dwell, emphasizing the collapse of Nineveh’s former strength and security under God’s judgment.

questions.question: How does Nahum 2:12's description of the lion tearing prey for his whelps and filling his dens relate to God's sovereignty over nations?
options: It depicts the former dominance of Nineveh and foreshadows its removal by divine decree
It teaches that nations are independent of God’s control
It symbolizes the nurturing care of God
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts the former dominance of Nineveh and foreshadows its removal by divine decree
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:12 uses the lion’s past dominance as a metaphor for Nineveh’s power, which God will overturn, affirming divine sovereignty over nations.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated in Nahum 2:13 where He declares burning chariots and devouring the young lions?
options: God’s righteous wrath and judgment against evil
questions.correctAnswer: God’s righteous wrath and judgment against evil
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:13 reveals God’s active and fierce judgment against Nineveh, symbolized by burning chariots and devouring young lions, highlighting His righteousness and wrath.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Nahum 2:6 and Nahum 2:13 provide about God's control over history and judgment?
options: God sovereignly orchestrates the fall of oppressive powers and judges them decisively
God leaves human history to chance
God is indifferent to political affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly orchestrates the fall of oppressive powers and judges them decisively
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:6 describes the palace dissolving, and 2:13 shows God burning chariots and devouring lions, together affirming God's sovereign judgment over nations and history.

questions.question: How does the combination of Nahum 2:1 and Nahum 2:5 deepen our understanding of human responsibility and divine sovereignty in judgment?
options: Humans are called to prepare and strengthen themselves, yet ultimately judgment is under God's sovereign control
Humans alone determine the outcome of battles
Humans have no role in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are called to prepare and strengthen themselves, yet ultimately judgment is under God's sovereign control
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:1 commands preparation and strength, while 2:5 shows the worthies stumbling, teaching that human effort is necessary but God's sovereign will determines the outcome.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Bible portrays God as unjust in His destruction of Nineveh. What does Nahum 2:2-3 actually teach about God's justice and holiness?
options: God’s judgment is a response to the emptiers who have corrupted and marred, demonstrating His justice and holiness
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is a response to the emptiers who have corrupted and marred, demonstrating His justice and holiness
questions.explanation: Nahum 2:2-3 shows God turning away the excellency of Israel because of corruption, and the red shields symbolize righteous wrath, emphasizing divine justice and holiness.
